**Michelson-Morley Experiment:**
An optical interferometer experiment conducted in 1887 to detect the relative motion of Earth through the hypothetical stationary luminiferous aether (the assumed medium for light wave propagation).

**Main Conclusion:**
The experiment yielded a null result—there was no detectable fringe shift indicating motion relative to the aether. 
*Conclusion:* The speed of light in vacuum is invariant (constant) in all inertial frames of reference, independent of the motion of the source or observer. This disproved the aether theory and paved the way for Einstein's Special Theory of Relativity.
proTip: The null result of the Michelson-Morley experiment is one of the most famous negative results in physics history.
